proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is longer/variable or admissions reflect severity dynamics rather than timing alone, a fixed 1-week delay may misalign the peak and distort rise/decline symmetry.
proposals.rationale: Hospitalization-rate surveillance can lag infections; adding an exposed stage plus a short reporting/admission lag can better align a sharp seasonal peak without introducing an explicit hospitalization compartment that may be weakly identifiable in a 31-week training window.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May over-delay the signal, producing forecasts that peak too late and underfit early-season acceleration if admissions track infections more closely.
proposals.rationale: High peakiness and hospitalization semantics suggest a longer infection-to-admission delay may be needed; SEIR with a 2-week delay remains parsimonious while allowing peak timing to shift relative to the infectious proxy.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter tradeoffs (e.g., I→H vs H→R) and unstable peak height/width extrapolation.
proposals.rationale: Directly mapping observations to an explicit hospitalization compartment matches the target semantics (weekly hospitalization rate) and can capture sharper peaks via an additional transition stage, while remaining within allowed templates.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can blur mechanistic interpretation and inflate persistence (tail) if I and H contributions are not separable, potentially overpredicting post-peak levels.
proposals.rationale: If reported hospitalization rates partially reflect both current infectious burden and admissions (e.g., coding/aggregation effects), observing I+H can be a robust compromise that reduces reliance on precisely identifying H alone.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: With only 31 training weeks, waning may be unidentifiable and can mimic noise, causing spurious secondary rises or overly long tails.
proposals.rationale: Allows waning immunity/re-susceptibility within-season, which can help accommodate high-rate, high-peak series where decline may be slower than SEIR predicts; delayed_I aligns with admission lag without adding H.
